claims.statement: There is no minimal-length-encoding check: len7=0x7e with value 5 is accepted as a 5-byte frame.

claims.statement: len7 == 0x7f requires the high 32 bits of the 64-bit length (b2..b5) to be zero; otherwise WSConn::exit() is called and nothing is delivered.
The 64-bit length is assembled big-endian from b6..b9 and then narrowed with (long)(int), i.e. sign-extended from 32 bits.
Because of the (long)(int) narrowing a length of 0x80000000 becomes negative, is passed to recv_more as a huge unsigned value, and the frame therefore never completes (no crash, no error).
read_head first waits for 2 bytes (recv_more(this,2,...)) and only then parses the fixed header; partial headers leave the receive buffer untouched.

claims.statement: The unmasked body path waits for exactly payload_len bytes.
The masked body path waits for payload_len + 4 bytes (the four mask-key bytes are counted in-band).
Unmasking is byte-wise XOR: msg[old + i] = recvbuf[4 + i] ^ mask[i & 3], where old is the message length before this frame and i restarts at 0 for every frame.
Fragment payloads are appended at offset == current message length, so continuation fragments accumulate in arrival order.

claims.statement:
The 101 response is exactly 'HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
' + optional 'Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate
' + 'Sec-WebSocket-Accept: <28 chars>

', i.e. 129 bytes without the extension line and 175 with it.

With no key, a request whose first five bytes are 'GET /' and whose sixth byte is not '/' gets a 19-byte 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\n\r\n' and the path (bytes from index 5 up to space/CR/LF) is passed to the second callback instead of being echoed.
'GET //...' (double slash after 'GET ') is rejected by discarding: zero bytes are produced and the receive handler is replaced with TcpConn::discard.

evidence.detail: pcVar17[5] != '/' is required for the 200 branch; otherwise control falls to the discard path

claims.statement: A request whose method is not GET (e.g. POST) is rejected with zero bytes.
If two adjacent '.' bytes occur while extracting the 200-OK path, the whole path is cleared (assigned the empty string) while the 200 response is still sent.
Without a '\r\n\r\n' in the buffer the handshake does nothing and waits for more data.
recv_pat invokes the callback with the INDEX of the pattern inside the receive buffer (ptr - buf), not with a length or an end offset.

claims.statement: recv_more is a pure unsigned comparison: ready iff need <= buffered bytes; equality is ready.
Arriving bytes are appended to the receive buffer and the pattern wait is re-run, so a frame may be split across arbitrarily many chunks.
A null incoming Buffer calls WSConn::exit(); an empty (but non-null) buffer simply appends nothing.

There is no explicit protocol state machine: every arrival re-derives progress from 'are there enough bytes at the head of the buffer', and consumed bytes are removed with memmove, which is what makes pipelining work.

evidence.detail: read_head always restarts at the buffer head
header bytes are memmove'd out, remainder kept
payload+mask bytes are memmove'd out, remainder kept

claims.inference_basis: the absence of a state enum/field is observed; calling this 'no state machine' is an architectural interpretation
